coverage: CATCH-UP EDITION covering THREE missed sessions — Wednesday 12, Thursday 13 and Friday 14 August. The last brief was 12 August: the headless research job has aborted on an expired login every morning since, so five days of email went out carrying stale content. Latest completed session everywhere is FRIDAY 14 AUG; SGX and HKEX opened this morning but Monday marks are not in here. Written 13:00 SGT, later than usual because the run had to be redone after a date error.
tldr: THE WEEK'S DEFINING FACT IS A NEGATIVE. It delivered two benign inflation prints — July CPI exactly on consensus at 3.4%/2.5%, then July PPI FLAT against +0.2% expected — and the long end gave ZERO net relief. The 10Y rallied 5bp Thursday and handed every basis point back Friday to close at exactly its Wednesday level, 4.68%. Both auctions cleared at multi-decade highs WITH demand present ($42bn of 10s at 4.683%, highest since 2007, dealers left only 8.6%; $25bn of 30s at 5.216%, highest since 2001). Buyers turned up and the curve still would not richen on good news — a term-premium problem, not a buyers' strike.

A CORRECTION TO SOMETHING I'VE TOLD YOU REPEATEDLY: the 30-year has NOT been breaking out to post-2007 highs. Verified against the official Treasury curve, the 2026 peak is 5.27% set on 31 JULY; Friday closed 5.25%, two basis points below it, and it has chopped in a 5.09-5.27 band for three weeks. A stalled long end is a materially less hostile backdrop for your REITs and developers than an accelerating one.

YOUR LARGEST RISK IS MAKING LOWER HIGHS. Silver has now failed three times: it peaked at 66.82 on Wednesday BEFORE the CPI release, then made successively lower highs of 66.31 and 65.72, never printed a 67 handle, and closed the week at 64.68 — up just 1.74%, or +2.78% at 1.6x. Metal that cannot hold gains across two friendly inflation prints is the signal, not the plus sign on the week.

READ YOUR BANK PRICES CAREFULLY TODAY. DBS's -1.07% on Friday was the S$0.81 dividend almost exactly — the underlying stock was FLAT, not down. And OCBC goes ex 47 cents THIS MORNING, roughly 1.48%. Across the two names that is ~2.5% of purely mechanical decline in consecutive sessions. Use S$31.32 as OCBC's adjusted reference, not Friday's S$31.79 close.

EXTREME DISPERSION IN HONG KONG. Tencent lost 4.68% over two sessions — Q2 revenue beat, but IFRS profit was FLAT at +0.7%, capex jumped 176% and free cash flow went NEGATIVE for the first time since 2005. Meanwhile SMIC ROSE 4.81% Friday against a -1.77% tech tape, on Q2 profit up 261.7% and Q3 margins guided higher again. The Hang Seng fell four straight sessions to a three-week low while mainland ChiNext rose 1.12% — Hong Kong-specific, not a China scare.

UNPRICED, AND IT HITS THIS MORNING: China's July new yuan loans CONTRACTED a record 340bn against +45bn expected, released after Friday's HK close. July activity data follows at 10:00 Beijing today. Two-sided — bad growth, higher stimulus odds — into a market already at a three-week low.

The US consumer rolled over on Friday: retail sales -0.6% against +0.1% expected, the worst since May 2025, with the GDP-relevant control group at -0.4%. Michigan sentiment fell to 51.0 from 55.2 while year-ahead inflation expectations ROSE to 4.3%. Equities ignored it — the S&P set a record Thursday, the Russell closed at a fresh record Friday, and the VIX made its lowest close of 2026.

UOL is the genuine damage in Singapore: -8.75% across Thursday and Friday with NO dividend or corporate action to excuse it, on a 7% revenue decline masked by fair-value gains. Mark it as a real loss. Singtel is the mirror image — it sold off on a -71.6% headline then reversed +4.71% once the underlying 11.4% consensus beat was digested.

The run was initially framed on a WRONG DATE — it believed the day was Thursday 13 Aug. Its own verification agents caught and refuted that using the machine clock, three vendor date stamps and an exact reference-close chain, and the research was redone against the true frame.

RESOLVED: the flat S-REIT prints were SGX TICK SIZE, not a stale feed. One tick is 0.5-0.85% on those four names, so 0.00% is the expected print. No vendor swap needed — and the inverse now holds: any sub-0.5% non-zero change on them IS a data error.

regime.label: Disinflation confirmed twice, and the long end still would not rally
regime.oneLiner: Two benign inflation prints produced zero net duration relief, silver made a third failed breakout, and the US consumer rolled over — while equities set records and volatility hit its 2026 low.

topNews.headline: Silver's third failed breakout: two successive lower highs after Wednesday's 66.82 peak, never a 67 handle, +1.74% on the week
topNews.actionable: +2.78% at 1.6x is positive but less than the closes suggest, and the structure deteriorated every session. The pattern is now established — silver rallies into a catalyst, tops at or before the release, and bleeds after. Watch 66.82; until it clears, every rally is a lower high.

topNews.headline: Zero net duration relief across a week of good inflation news — 10Y round-tripped to 4.68%, both auctions cleared at multi-decade highs with demand present
topNews.actionable: A term-premium problem rather than a demand problem, which keeps structural pressure on the S-REITs and developers even as the hike risk recedes.

topNews.headline: CORRECTION: the 30Y has not broken out — 2026 peak is 5.27% set 31 July, Friday closed 5.25%
topNews.actionable: Materially less hostile for the duration-sensitive sleeve than the narrative I had been running. Do not treat a 5.27% vendor print as a new high.

topNews.headline: Tencent: revenue beat but IFRS profit flat, capex +176%, free cash flow negative for the first time since 2005 — down 4.68% over two sessions to HK$440.00
topNews.actionable: Demand is fine and the adjusted profit line hit consensus; the cash profile is what changed. That is a re-rating question, not a demand question.

topNews.headline: SMIC is the book's standout: Q2 profit +261.7%, stock +4.81% Friday to HK$70.80 against a -1.77% tech tape
topNews.actionable: It beat its own guidance and guided Q3 margins higher, and it rose on a session when peer Hua Hong fell 11.55% despite its own beat. Company-specific execution, not a sector bid.

topNews.headline: China's July new yuan loans contracted a RECORD 340bn — released after Friday's HK close, so unpriced into this morning
topNews.actionable: The live catalyst today, alongside July activity data at 10:00 Beijing, into a Hang Seng already at a three-week low after four down sessions.

topNews.headline: DBS's Friday drop was the dividend, not a decline — and OCBC goes ex 47 cents this morning
topNews.actionable: ~2.5% of mechanical decline across the two bank lines in consecutive sessions. The dangerous inverse: if a genuine selloff coincides with today's ex-date, do not write it off as 'just the dividend'.

signals: The single most important read of the week: two disinflationary prints could not move the long end. If good inflation news cannot rally duration, the constraint on your REIT and developer sleeve is term premium, not the Fed path — and that does not resolve with a soft CPI.

Silver's failure is now a pattern rather than an event. Three catalysts, three highs made at or before the release, three fades. The levered position gained on the week and still deteriorated technically, which is exactly the configuration that lulls you before a margin event.

The consumer/equity divergence is stark: retail sales control group negative and sentiment at 51.0, against an S&P record, a Russell record and a 2026-low VIX. One of those is wrong. Positioning for which is a decision, not an observation.

Inside HK the sleeve has stopped moving as one — Tencent -4.68% and SMIC +4.81% in the same two sessions. That is healthy for stock-picking and bad for anyone treating the three names as one China-tech exposure.

Miner economics are being misread industry-wide. Barrick's costs rose 20% and its unit margin still expanded 58%, because realised gold rose 34%. Expect the same shape from Newmont. The cost headlines are true and the conclusion drawn from them is backwards.
